auto_merge.commit_title: [Pooling] Speed up ColBERT reranking with batched token heads (#64269)

repo.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
repo.name: vllm

detail.body:
## Purpose

Batch token-embedding casts and projections across requests, then finish slicing and normalization per request only when their settings differ. This removes repeated ColBERT head launches without adding kernels or GPU-specific tuning.

## Claims

- Higher ColBERT throughput with matching settings; mixed dimensions/normalization now also share projection.
- Late chunking, chunked prefill and batch-invariant execution retain the existing path and output ownership. This complements #62940's task-dispatch optimization.

## Validation

**Latest refactor, main → branch:** `answerdotai/answerai-colbert-small-v1`, MRV2, BF16 backbone/FP32 head, TP1, eager. 32 documents plus a query per request, L128, C32, four API workers. H100 and B300 each used two fresh-server runs per variant in balanced order, 256 warmups and 4,096 timed requests/run; all **32,768 NVIDIA requests succeeded**. The MI355X row is from a separate AMD rerun and is not included in that request count. Values are per-metric medians.

| GPU | Requests/s | Gain | p50 ms | p99 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 | 138.26 → 193.91 | +40.2% | 228.87 → 163.23 | 289.60 → 217.28 |
| B300 | 181.62 → 242.00 | +33.2% | 172.12 → 129.61 | 208.45 → 155.49 |
| MI355X | 204.15 → 331.89 | +62.6% | 156.18 → 92.08 | 197.30 → 134.16 |

**Accuracy:** the latest code passes the existing ColBERT/HF comparison on H100. On H100 and B300, eight real-model requests mixing normalized and raw outputs match main, including norms (maximum absolute error **7.15e-7**). The 48 head cases on each of those two GPUs also cover mixed dimensions, late chunking, batch-invariant mode and buffer reuse (maximum absolute error **1.19e-6**, `atol=2e-6, rtol=1e-4`).

**Earlier SciFact evaluation (not rerun for this refactor):** BM25 top-50 reranking, 300 queries / 5,183 documents. HF FP32 reference: NDCG@10 **0.73519**, MRR@10 **0.71167**.

| GPU | NDCG@10, main → branch | MRR@10, main → branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| H100 | 0.73143 → 0.73143 | 0.70707 → 0.70707 |
| B300 | 0.73185 → 0.73185 | 0.70757 → 0.70757 |

## Details

**Tests:** 124 pooling/head/late-interaction cases pass on each of H100 and B300; local pre-commit checks also pass. Three compact CPU cases check projection count and output parity; the existing ownership test also covers an identity head. The previous PR implementation fails the two mixed-setting projection-count checks; the updated implementation passes. Four added cases overall, no new test file or CI job.

<details>
<summary>Commands, variability and earlier measurements</summary>

Checkpoint revision: `934fa8bb4ce2284f4c2baa232d81aca4d076fa5e`; cached at `/tmp/colbert-model`. Each pair uses a fixed main baseline and the same installed wheel, model, hardware and flags. Set GPU visibility and NUMA-local CPU affinity; OMP threads 4, seed 20261028. CPUs were not reserved.

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main \
  serve /tmp/colbert-model --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18671 --served-model-name colbert \
  --runner pooling --dtype bfloat16 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 512 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 \
  --disable-log-requests --api-server-count 4

OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --backend vllm-rerank --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18671 --endpoint /rerank \
  --model /tmp/colbert-model --served-model-name colbert --dataset-name random-rerank \
  --no-reranker --random-input-len 128 --random-range-ratio 0 --random-batch-size 33 \
  --num-prompts 131073 --max-concurrency 32 --request-rate inf --seed 20261028 \
  --num-warmups 256 --disable-tqdm --save-result --save-detailed \
  --percentile-metrics e2el --metric-percentiles 50,99
```

Throughput ranges: H100 **136.20–140.33 → 191.91–195.91**, B300 **181.12–182.12 → 241.99–242.02 requests/s**. Maximum observed request latency: H100 **371.29 → 296.22 ms**, B300 **250.77 → 251.90 ms**. Benchmark accounting includes the shared query: 132 effective tokens per document for the L128 setting.

**Output on main / branch, verbatim** (one H100 run each):
```text
{"label": "final-api4-c32-d32-l128-0-main", "duration": 30.073361448012292, "completed": 4096, "request_throughput": 136.20027169495967, "mean_e2el_ms": 233.64472467618924, "median_e2el_ms": 231.79334800806828, "p99_e2el_ms": 291.5200556541095}
{"label": "final-api4-c32-d32-l128-1-branch", "duration": 20.9077028480242, "completed": 4096, "request_throughput": 195.90865767384273, "mean_e2el_ms": 162.35997553364712, "median_e2el_ms": 161.51539450220298, "p99_e2el_ms": 215.5416862005952}
```

**Test plan:**

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_heads.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_methods.py tests/v1/worker/test_late_interaction_runner.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  'tests/models/language/pooling/test_colbert.py::test_colbert_hf_comparison[bert-v2]' -q
```

The H100/B300 real-model mixed-normalization comparisons also passed with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

**Additional workloads and AMD reruns:** A uses the setup above. B uses 8 documents, L32, C8, one API worker and 32 warmups. The H100/B300 B rows are earlier measurements, before the latest refactor, with three fresh-server runs per variant and 4,096 requests/run. The MI355X A/B rows are latest-refactor reruns.

| GPU / workload | Requests/s | Gain | p50 ms | p99 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 / B | 226.23 → 254.47 | +12.5% | 34.61 → 30.56 | 43.04 → 40.66 |
| B300 / B | 232.71 → 255.52 | +9.8% | 34.12 → 30.87 | 42.69 → 37.66 |
| MI355X / A (latest refactor rerun) | 204.15 → 331.89 | +62.6% | 156.18 → 92.08 | 197.30 → 134.16 |
| MI355X / B (latest refactor rerun) | 365.11 → 391.54 | +7.2% | 21.64 → 21.12 | 25.80 → 23.29 |

For B, omit `--api-server-count`; use input length 32, batch size 9, prompts 32769, concurrency 8 and warmups 32.

</details>

### AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-6) drafted the code. All changed lines were human-reviewed and relevant tests were human-run.

+    metadata = _make_metadata(lengths, pooling_params=params)
+    expected = [
+        head.forward_chunk(chunk, param)
+        for chunk, param in zip(hidden.split(lengths), params, strict=True)
+    ]
+    projections, activations = [], []
+    with (
+        projector.register_forward_hook(
+            lambda _module, _inputs, output: projections.append(output)
+        ),
+        activation.register_forward_hook(
+            lambda _module, _inputs, output: activations.append(output)
+        ),
+    ):
+        outputs = pooler(hidden, metadata)
+    for actual, reference in zip(outputs, expected, strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, reference)
+    assert len(projections) == 1
+    assert len(activations) == expected_calls
+

+    def forward_batched(
+        self,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        pooling_params: list[PoolingParams],
+        split: Callable[[torch.Tensor], list[TokenPoolingMethodOutputItem]],
+    ) -> list[TokenPoolerHeadOutputItem] | None:
+        """Batch projection, splitting only when finishing needs per-request options.
+
+        Keep eligibility checks in sync with PoolingParams fields read by forward_chunk.
+        """
+        if envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT or any(
+            p.late_chunking_params is not None for p in pooling_params
+        ):
+            return None
+        # [total_tokens, hidden_size] -> [total_tokens, embedding_size]
+        embeddings = self._project(hidden_states)
+        first = pooling_params[0]
+        if all(
+            p.dimensions == first.dimensions
+            and p.use_activation == first.use_activation
+            for p in pooling_params
+        ):
+            embeddings = self._finish(embeddings, first)
+            # Each output has shape [request_tokens, output_size].
+            return split(embeddings)
+        # Each part has shape [request_tokens, embedding_size].
+        pooled_data = split(embeddings)
+        del embeddings
+        return [
+            self._finish(part, param) if part is not None else None
+            for part, param in zip(pooled_data, pooling_params, strict=True)
+        ]
+
+    def _project(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Project [num_rows, hidden_size] to [num_rows, embedding_size]."""
+        if self.head_dtype is not None:
+            hidden_states = hidden_states.to(self.head_dtype)
+        if self.projector is not None:
+            return self.projector(hidden_states)
+        return hidden_states
+
+    def _finish(
+        self, embeddings: torch.Tensor, pooling_param: PoolingParams
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Slice/normalize [num_rows, embedding_size] to [num_rows, output_size]."""
+        if pooling_param.dimensions is not None:
+            embeddings = embeddings[..., : pooling_param.dimensions]
+        if self.activation is not None and pooling_param.use_activation:
+            embeddings = self.activation(embeddings)
+        return embeddings

We could support this by batching the head only for requests that finish in each step, either here or in a follow-up PR.
